summary: CUDA decode, speculative verify and varlen causal prefill attention for a ragged batch of sequences whose BF16 or E4M3 KV pages are addressed through Core StateCache block tables, with a launch shape independent of lengths and a deterministic split-key combine
implementation_scope: CUDA source for head dimensions 64, 128 and 256 with grouped-query heads: a write kernel storing a step's rows at Round::kv slots (BF16 copy or E4M3 with per-head-vector scales); decode over (key/value head, block, sequence) blocks merging strided 128-key pieces gathered through block tables, two key streams per block, BF16 tensor cores, an FP32 online softmax and a fixed-order combine, with up to 64 rows (verify columns times grouped query heads) per sequence and key/value head; varlen causal prefill with 128-query blocks over a paged prefix plus new keys; DevicePages (StateStorage copy-on-write as 2-D device copies for every layer) and BatchTables (block tables, lengths, query offsets and write slots in one device buffer); a host model of addressing, ragged batches and the combine. Projections, rotary embedding, scheduling and the StateCache itself are engine or Core supplied. Sliding windows, per-head sinks, soft-caps and verify tree masks are launch parameters; decode walks only the pieces inside the window and keeps column invariance.

agent_guidance.use_when: An engine batches several requests per step (concurrent requests, mixed decode and prefill batches, speculative verify) or reuses prompt prefixes and forks across requests, and its KV lives in Core's StateCache pages
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The engine serves one contiguous sequence (fp8-kv-attention or flash-prefill-attention fit it), the model has no softmax attention, head dimensions are not 64, 128 or 256, or a sequence needs more than 64 decode rows per key/value head
provides: Sliding windows read through Core's window_table without touching passed (no_page) pages, per-head sinks, soft-caps and tree masks for speculative token-tree verification
Physical-row addressing page * page_tokens + offset shared by every attention layer, with tiles gathered row by row so any page size works
A write kernel for a step's new rows at Core's Round::kv slots, BF16 or E4M3 with one scale per row and key/value head
Decode and multi-column verify for a ragged batch in one launch whose shape depends only on host counts (sequences, blocks, columns), with idle slots for padded graph batch sizes

Deterministic split-key decode: strided 128-key pieces per block, two key streams per block and a combine in (block, stream) order; columns alone equal verify columns and sequences alone equal batched ones bit for bit
Varlen causal prefill over a paged prefix plus new keys with ragged query counts per sequence
DevicePages, a StateStorage whose copy_rows copies a page's rows in every layer, and BatchTables, which packs a step's tables, lengths, query offsets and slots
A host model of block-table addressing, ragged batches and the split-key combine
engine_supplies: Queries and keys after normalization and rotary embedding, keys written before the attention that reads them
The StateCache configuration (page_tokens equal to the pages', prefix identity naming the KV representation) and one thread for its calls
Blocks per sequence and key/value head chosen from the device's SM count, the partial buffer and the batch bounds
retire() after the kernels that read released pages, and whole-model quality measurement when choosing E4M3 pages
preserve: Writes only at Round::kv slots; shared and indexed pages stay immutable and copy-on-write goes through copy_rows
A tile after a row's position leaves that row's maximum, sum and output unchanged
Piece-to-block and tile-to-stream assignment and the combine order depend only on key positions
Decode work grows with the tokens held, not with the capacity or the table length
E4M3 scales per row and key/value head, applied when a tile is dequantized
adapt: Tile, piece and block sizes, key streams per block and rows per decode block
Page layout (head-major pages, separate K and V pools) and table width
Prefill block size, other head dimensions and E4M3 tensor-core prompt attention as in fp8-kv-attention

code_files.purpose: Page and batch layouts and the write, decode and prefill interfaces
Write, varlen prefill, two-stream split-key decode and combine kernels for head dimensions 64, 128 and 256, BF16 and E4M3 pages
DevicePages (StateStorage over device pages of every layer) and BatchTables (one step's tables, lengths, offsets and slots)
Host model of block-table addressing, ragged batches and the ordered split-key combine

requires.hardware: CUDA C++20 on sm_80+ (BF16 mma.sync, ldmatrix, cp.async; E4M3 conversions are native from sm_89 and emulated before), up to 96 KiB of shared memory per block at head dimension 256; builds checked for sm_80, sm_86, sm_89 and sm_120, runtime validation on sm_120 only; Python 3.11+ standard library for the reference
requires.model: Softmax attention with grouped-query (or multi-head) key/value heads and head dimension 64, 128 or 256
requires.workload: Concurrent requests, prefix reuse, forks and speculative verify with up to 64 rows per sequence and key/value head

contract.input: BF16 key/value rows and int32 physical-row slots for write; BF16 queries [rows][q_stride], the pages, device block tables, kv_lens and q_start, head counts, score scale, max_columns and blocks for decode (max_queries for prefill)
contract.output: BF16 values or E4M3 codes and FP32 scales in the pages; FP32 attention output [rows][out_stride] per query head
contract.ownership: The engine owns queries, pages, tables, scratch and output; launches borrow them on the caller stream. DevicePages owns its allocations; the StateCache owns page lifetimes
contract.failure: Null buffers, non-positive sizes, heads not a multiple of key/value heads, unaligned or short strides, unsupported head dimensions, E4M3 pages without scales, more than 64 decode rows per key/value head, blocks outside 1..1024 or more than 65,535 sequences return cudaErrorInvalidValue; launch errors are returned. Device counts the launch cannot see are a contract: a sequence with more queries than max_columns (decode) or max_queries (prefill), more queries than its kv_len, or a kv_len beyond table_stride * page_tokens reads no keys, gets NaN in every row and head, and sets the optional Batch::fault flag to 1. DevicePages and BatchTables throw on bad geometry, exceeded bounds and CUDA errors
contract.core_boundary: No Core change: the pages implement Core's StateStorage and read Core's block tables; Core never touches page bytes

dependencies: CUDA runtime with cuda_bf16.h and cuda_fp8.h
Python standard library for the reference

validation.host: The README example: addressing through a block table, split-key decode with 1 and 3 blocks equal within 1e-12, a verify column equal to the same column alone
validation.native: Core StateCache with prefix caching, ragged prefills (64, 300, 130, 9 after 64 reused rows, 1), a copy-on-write fork, idle slots, 3-column verifies and decode across page boundaries for head dimensions 64/128/256 and BF16/E4M3 pages, against the attention-state CPU reference within 2^-8 of the output magnitude (at most 2.6e-3 on sm_120); E4M3 codes and scales equal to a host encoder; verify columns, lone sequences and captured graph replays bit for bit equal to their references; invalid problems rejected; sequences whose device counts break the batch (too many queries, more queries than keys, a short table) NaN with the fault flag set in decode and prefill; windowed prefill and a tree verify with sinks and soft-caps for BF16 and E4M3 pages against an FP64 reference with every passed page pointing at NaN, and windowed columns alone bit for bit equal to the verify (attention_variants_tests.cu)
validation.performance: RTX 5090 (1,438 GB/s probed), 4,096 keys, head dimension 128, 32/8 heads, shuffled 16-token pages: 64 sequences decode in 0.80 ms with BF16 pages (1,336 GB/s of KV read) and 0.57 ms with E4M3 pages (974 GB/s); one sequence in 26 us (BF16) and 32 us (E4M3) against 36 us for the contiguous fp8-kv-attention decode in the same run; no claim for other devices or shapes
